key.name: dictation-enabled
key.description: Master switch -- when false, the hotkey is never grabbed at all.

key.name: hotkey
key.description: Held to record, released to transcribe+paste -- recorded with the Settings app's Peach Intelligence tab using the exact same ShortcutRow widget/UX as peachySearch's own shortcut picker, so any real accelerator (a bare modifier, or a full Ctrl/Alt/ Super chord) is fair game, not a fixed list. Main.wm.addKeybinding's expected array-of-accelerators type. hotkey-trigger-keyval/hotkey-modifier-mask below are the pre-parsed form the extension actually uses to detect release -- kept in sync whenever this changes; never edit this key directly without also updating those.

key.name: hotkey-trigger-keyval
key.summary: Parsed base keyval of 'hotkey' (Gtk.accelerator_parse's own output)
key.description: The extension can't safely parse an arbitrary accelerator string itself -- Gdk/Gtk aren't available inside gnome-shell's own process, only in a prefs.js (a separate, ordinary GTK process; confirmed no other extension in this repo imports Gdk from its own extension.js) -- so the Settings app pre-parses 'hotkey' with Gtk.accelerator_parse and writes the result here + hotkey-modifier-mask. Default 100 = 'd', matching the default hotkey above.

key.name: hotkey-modifier-mask
key.description: Companion to hotkey-trigger-keyval. Numerically identical to Clutter's own ModifierType bits -- both wrap the same X11/xkbcommon modifier layout (confirmed: SHIFT=1, LOCK=2, CONTROL=4, ALT=8, SUPER=67108864 in both) -- so the extension compares it directly against live Clutter modifier state (global.get_pointer()'s own mods) with no translation needed. Default 12 = Control(4)|Alt(8), matching the default hotkey.

key.name: cleanup-enabled
key.summary: Clean up transcriptions with an AI provider
key.description: When true, the raw transcript is sent to cleanup-provider (via the API key stored in the login keyring, never here) for punctuation/grammar/filler-word cleanup before pasting. When false (or no key is stored), the raw whisper.cpp transcript is pasted as-is -- dictation itself never requires an API key, only this optional cleanup pass.

key.name: cleanup-provider
key.summary: Which provider's API key to use for cleanup

key.name: recording-state
key.summary: Live push-to-talk state, for the Dynamic Island to display
key.description: 'idle', 'listening', 'transcribing', or 'error' -- written by this extension on every state change (hotkey press/release, and Paste()/Failed() called back by the daemon). macos-top-panel@local.dev's Dynamic Island (lib/dynamicIsland.js) watches this key instead of the two extensions sharing an actor directly, so either can be enabled/disabled/reloaded independently. This extension no longer draws its own recording indicator -- see extension.js's own comment on _grabAnchor for why a (now invisible) actor is still needed regardless.
